text: Upcoming: ACCL is hosting the mini-symposium “Systems-Theoretic Approaches to Learning V” at the SIAM Conference on Mathematics of Data Science (MDS26), Salt Lake City, UT (November 18, 2026).
Our paper on a chemistry-transferable physics-informed neural network surrogate for Li-ion cells with online continual learning was accepted in the Journal of Energy Storage.
Our paper on hierarchical multi-scale graph neural networks (Hossen & Sahoo) appeared at ICML 2026, Seoul, South Korea, a top-tier machine learning conference.
Two papers presented at the European Control Conference (ECC 2026), Iceland: Laplacian-based modeling of thermal interactions in battery packs, and co-synthesis of communication and control for CPS.
Our paper “Stealthy reward poisoning in continuous-time LTI systems: Exploiting algebraic Riccati structure in integral IRL” was accepted to IEEE CDC 2026, Honolulu, HI.
Dr. Sahoo organized the invited session “Systems-Theoretic Approaches to Learning IV” at IEEE WCCI 2026, Maastricht, the Netherlands.
Two papers presented at IJCNN 2026 (WCCI), Maastricht: safe adaptive output tracking for robotic manipulators, and resource-constrained safe RL for lane following of wheeled mobile robots.
Dr. Sahoo returned to Idaho National Laboratory for his summer faculty fellowship.
Saima traveled to Idaho National Laboratory for a summer research visit at INL.
Our paper on sparse-frequency EIS measurements and impedance spectrum reconstruction for Li-ion cell modeling was presented at ACC 2026, New Orleans, LA.
“Maximizing unlabeled data utility with improved representation learning and pseudo labeling” was published in the IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society.
Invited talk by Dr. Sahoo, “Resource-aware and safe intelligent control with guaranteed approximation accuracy,” Department of ECE, Auburn University (Feb 9, 2026).
“Safe data-enabled control of human-in-the-loop robotic manipulator systems” was published in IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics.
Our paper on resource-efficient distributed quantum learning over wireless networks with qubit reuse was presented at IEEE CCNC 2026, Las Vegas, NV.
“State-constrained online adaptive control for robotic manipulators” was published in IEEE Control Systems Letters.
Our paper on an online pseudospectral approach for system identification and state estimation was presented at IEEE CDC 2025, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
“MetaRep: Improving meta-learning accuracy by learning episodic representation” was accepted in the International Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics.
Dr. Sahoo organized the invited session “Systems-Theoretic Approaches to Learning II: Applications to System Identification, State Estimation, and Control” at IEEE IJCNN 2025, Rome, Italy.
Two papers presented at IJCNN 2025, Rome, Italy: REAL-PINN for real-time battery health prediction, and contrastive learning for triage of cloud security alerts.
Our paper on online system identification using Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind was presented at the American Control Conference (ACC 2025), Denver, CO.
Dr. Sahoo began a summer faculty fellowship at Idaho National Laboratory (INL).
Sazzad traveled to Idaho National Laboratory for a summer research visit as part of our NSF project.
Our NSF REU paper on multidisciplinary collaborative undergraduate research was presented at the ASEE Annual Conference, Montreal, Canada.
Dr. Sahoo organized the mini-symposium “System Theoretic Approach to Learning III” at the SIAM Conference on Applications of Dynamical Systems (DS25), Denver, CO (May 12, 2025).

Saima Alam and Md. Sazzad Hossen were each renewed for a second year of the Alabama EPSCoR Graduate Research Scholars Program, with Dr. Sahoo as PI. Sazzad: graph neural networks for Li-ion battery management systems; Saima: Li-ion battery pack modeling and identification.
“DenoMAE: A multimodal autoencoder for denoising modulation signals” was published in IEEE Communications Letters.

Invited talk by Dr. Sahoo, “Real-time learning embedded next generation of battery management systems for electric vehicle safety,” AI Institute, Department of CSE, University of South Carolina (Mar 28, 2025).
Invited talk by Dr. Sahoo, “Revolutionizing electric vehicle safety: The next generation of battery management systems,” Department of ECE, North Dakota State University (Jan 23, 2025).
Our paper on federated split learning for human activity recognition with differential privacy was presented at IEEE CCNC 2025, Las Vegas, NV.
Our paper on aperiodic sensing and data-driven system identification using a Chebyshev pseudospectral approach was presented at IEEE CDC 2024, Milan, Italy.
Our paper “BEpiC: Binary episodes for meta-learning towards better generalization” was presented at WOCC 2024, Hsinchu, Taiwan.

Two talks at the SIAM Conference on Mathematics of Data Science (MDS24), Atlanta, GA: continual learning in Li-ion battery management systems, and interpretable inference of drift and control vector fields of stochastic dynamical systems.
Talk at the ECS Meeting, Honolulu, HI: “Learning lithium-ion battery health in real-time.”

Congratulations to Saima Alam and Md. Sazzad Hossen on receiving Alabama EPSCoR Graduate Research Scholars Program (GRSP) awards. Sazzad: graph neural networks for Li-ion battery management systems; Saima: Li-ion battery pack modeling and identification.
Md. Sazzad Hossen was awarded the UAH Ventre Fellowship in Engineering for new Ph.D. students.
Invited talk by Dr. Sahoo, “Resource-aware optimal control for cyber-physical systems,” ECE Department, University of Alabama, Tuscaloosa (Aug 28, 2024).
Our paper on public healthcare informatics for COVID-19 from social media data was presented at IEEE EMBC 2024, Orlando, FL.
New NSF SaTC award (#2337999, collaborative with the University of South Carolina): Vulnerability Characterization of Learning-Based Controllers in Networked Cyber-Physical Systems.
Sazzad presented his paper on multi-label defect classification using graph neural networks at IEEE WCCI.
UAH News covers our NSF EPSCoR fellowship on preventing catastrophic failures in EV lithium-ion battery packs.
Dr. Sahoo invited to serve as a panelist for National Science Foundation proposal review.
Dr. Sahoo presented Geetika's work on self-learning EV battery management systems at the International Mechatronics Conference, Oklahoma City.
Sazzad presented Graph Neural Networks for Defect Classification at the International Mechatronics Conference, Oklahoma City.
Dr. Sahoo joined IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems (TNNLS) as Associate Editor.
Welcome to new members Sophia Lopez (UG RA), Tiffany Lodge (Ph.D.), Jessica Hamer (M.S.), Mahtab Noor Shaan (M.S.), and Saima Alam (Ph.D.).
Presented core temperature estimation of Li-ion batteries under internal thermal faults using neural networks at CCTA, Bridgetown, Barbados.
NSF funding for a collaborative REU Site on Smart Personal Protective Equipment.
Naval Surface Warfare Center (DoD) funding for Towards Autonomy in Uncertain Environments: Exploring Vistas Beyond Consensus.
Learning-based faulty state estimation paper accepted in IEEE Transactions on Transportation Electrification.
Core temperature estimation paper accepted for presentation at CCTA 2023.
Department of Energy funding for AI-enabled Autonomy of Robotic Inspection Platforms for Sustainability of Energy Infrastructure.
Md. Sazzad Hossen (Ph.D.) joined ACCL.
OCAST second-year funding for Meta and Multimodal Learning for Smart Visual Borescope Inspection.
Congratulations to Geetika Vennam on defending her Ph.D. dissertation; she joins Idaho National Laboratory as a Postdoctoral Fellow.
A dynamic SOH-coupled lithium-ion cell model accepted in IEEE Transactions on Energy Conversion.
Survey on Li-ion battery degradation modeling and SOH estimation accepted in the Journal of Energy Storage.
OCAST funding for Meta and Multimodal Learning for Smart Visual Borescope Inspection.
TranSET (US DOT) funding for an Intelligent Incipient Fault Detection System for EV Batteries.
TranSET (US DOT) funding for Smart Battery Management Systems for Electric Vehicles.
